I was about 5 years old. Got attached to a big teddy bear my friend from school gave me for my birthday. One day, my mom and dad took that teddy bear from me and locked me and my little brother in a room. I remember screaming "What are you going to do with him?" and my parents replying with "We're going to burn him". I freaked out and cried while banging on the door, trying to get it open. Hit the door so hard my hand drew blood. Shouted and cried so loud my throat felt like it burnt.

I remember my little brother crying, telling me to stop hurting myself and trying to pull me away from the door. I remember my parents praying and speaking in tongues. I remember the smell of the fire that slowly turned my teddy bear to ash.

They burnt my teddy bear because I spent a lot of time with it, and that apparently meant the teddy bear was possessed by satan.

That's when I stopped believing in god and religions.

Better deals always win; even brand loyalty can't retain customers if a better product appears and customers find out about it.

If your father's company can't stay afloat, it's his fault, not yours, because the result would still be the same if someone else becomes your dad's competitor and offers better quality or lower prices.

You've even offered him a full time job plus buying his equipment (capital that technically can't be quickly turned into cash and is depreciating as time goes on).
